text:
maria: Heads up — seeing a perf regression on mixtral-7b-v2 in the canary routing test. Per-token latency up ~18% for chat requests that include a leading system message.

ajay: Can you paste the flamegraph/profile? sounds like KV warmup or kernel fallback.

maria: Pasting the hotspot from the internal profiler:

```
# hot paths (sample)
attn_byte_kernel  42.1%  (gkernel byte fallback)
kv_cache_lookup    18.7%
dispatcher/pick    12.4%  (kernel selection)
quant_ops          9.3%
other              17.5%
```

maria: Note: this only spikes for chat templates that include a ~200-char system prompt + an assistant history item. Non-chat single-turn gen is fine.

dave: quick thought — could be tokenizer causing byte-fallback and increasing token count. Emojis / special tokens in system message will trigger byte fallback on the tokenizer for some locales. That increases tokenization by ~20-30% and forces different kernel paths.

olivia: Also saw cases where kernel picker falls back to `attn_byte_kernel` when head/kvdim mismatch or quantization settings differ from the optimized build. We should verify kernel selection logs.

ajay: Can we get raw token counts + kernel decision per request? a small repro script would help.

maria: repro command I used:

```
./run_canary.sh --model mixtral-7b-v2 --route canary/chat --payload ./samples/system-heavy.json --profile --dump-kernels
```

maria: Kernel dump excerpt (per-request):
```
request_id=... kernel=attn_byte_kernel reason=token_byte_fallback
request_id=... kernel=optimized_attn reason=ok
```

ajay: proposing a quick tokenizer delta test. Run both tokenizers (byte fallback enabled vs disabled) on the same template:

```
# runtokenizer.py
from tokenizer_lib import Tokenizer
s = open('system-heavy.json').read()
for mode in ['byte_fallback_on','byte_fallback_off']:
    t = Tokenizer(mode=mode)
    toks = t.encode(s)
    print(mode, len(toks))
```


dave: ran that on my laptop — got 22% more tokens with byte_fallback_on. also noticed extra special BOS/EOS tokens when we use the chat template wrapper (we currently add an extra <|start|> for some legacy clients).

maria: that matches latency. So two compounding factors: increased token count (longer KV warmup) + kernel fallback to byte ops (slower attn kernel).

olivia: two immediate mitigation paths: 1) prevent kernel fallback by widening kernel picker compatibility (allow optimized_attn for kvdim/head variants if quant params ok) or 2) change batching heuristic to avoid grouping system-heavy templates into latency-sensitive fast-paths. I lean to (1) short term.

ajay: another option — pre-tokenize and add a small hint header with token_count estimate so router/batcher can choose smaller batch sizes or route to a different worker class. Pre-tokenizing also lets us avoid on-worker tokenizer overhead.

maria: agreed. For the canary I'd like a small experiment: 5% canary, two arms — A: kernel picker relaxed for mixtral-7b-v2 (force optimized_attn when compatible), B: pre-tokenize header + batch-by-estimated-tokens. Measure p50/p95 latency and token cost.

ben: infra can schedule. need commit hash, canary window, and which routes.

maria: commit c4f9b2a, canary 5% on `canary/chat`, run for 2 hours. Will attach the sample sets.

infra-bot: scheduled canary 1824003600 -> 1824007200 (5% traffic) for route canary/chat, image mixtral-7b-v2:c4f9b2a.

ajay: small note on RoPE scaling — if we change RoPE scaling factor for mixtral variants (we experimented with 1.02 earlier) it can change how memory access aligns and accidentally flip kernel heuristics (head stride detect). Olivia, did you see that?

olivia: yes — a RoPE scaling tweak previously made a few models prefer a slower kernel due to misalignment detection. Fix there was to normalize the axis rounding in the kernel picker. I'll push a patch to make the detection tolerant +/-1 byte so small RoPE deltas don't flip kernels.

maria: good. also let's add a small change to chat templates: remove redundant <|start|>/<|end|> when we already have assistant delimiters. That trimmed ~4 tokens in our local tests.

dave: will update the client template mapping in repo `chat-templates` and add a unit test asserting token_count delta < 2%.

ajay: summary of action items:
- olivia: kernel picker tolerance patch + PR
- dave: chat template cleanup + unit tests
- maria: run canary A/B and collect kernel decision + token_count traces
- ben/infra: schedule canary (done) and ensure trace retention 2h

maria: if the canary shows kernel fallback is the dominant cause we'll roll kernel picker patch to prod. If token_count / tokenizer is dominant we'll prioritize pre-tokenize header.

ben: got it, monitoring dashboards hooked up. I'll ping if any anomalies. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: canary started (5% traffic). collecting kernel & tokenizer traces to /canary_runs/1824000000/

maria: thanks all — keeping this thread for updates.
